heading: INT. BOTANICAL GARDEN, ORCHID HOUSE - NIGHT

units.text: INT. BOTANICAL GARDEN, ORCHID HOUSE - NIGHT
Mist hangs in humid air.
Violet and white blooms spill from hanging baskets.
A path of wet gravel winds between benches.
FENN, 40s, in a damp raincoat, crouches beside a bench and runs a gloved thumb along a stem.
CALLIOPE, 30s, the greenhouse curator, stands over him, arms folded, with a keyring that jingles at her hip.
He lifts a petal with tweezers.
She watches his hands.
This one's been cut.
units.name: FENN

units.text: Orchids are cut all the time.
units.name: CALLIOPE

units.text: Not at the root. Not with a scalpel.
units.name: FENN

units.text: She says nothing.
He bags the stem and places it carefully in a case.
You won't find anything here.
units.name: CALLIOPE

units.text: You're sure?
units.name: FENN

units.text: I'm certain.
units.name: CALLIOPE

units.text: He stands.
The mist parts around him.
He looks up at the glass ceiling, then back at her, and his eyes stop on her gloved hand.
Who taught you to hold a scalpel like that?
units.name: FENN

units.text: ^Who taught you to ask?
units.name: CALLIOPE

units.text: They speak in perfect unison.
A drop of water falls from a leaf onto the gravel.
Neither moves.
